final_answer: Ice floats on water due to the unique molecular structure of water. When water freezes, its molecules form a hexagonal crystalline lattice held together by hydrogen bonds. This arrangement creates open spaces between the molecules, making ice less dense than liquid water. Since density determines buoyancy, the lower density of ice allows it to float on the denser liquid water. This phenomenon is crucial for ecosystems, as it insulates bodies of water and supports life beneath the ice.
